{{nihongo|'''Gassan Shrine'''|月山神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Dewa Province]].

'''Gassan Shrine''' (がっさんじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located at the summit of {{ill|Mount Gassan|Q3174863|qid=Q3174863}} (elevation 1,984 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m}}) in {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|Q125863|qid=Q125863}}. It is a Shikinaisha listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}} in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'; under the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine rank system}}, it was the only {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kanpei Taisha}} in the {{ill|Tōhoku region|af|Tohoku|ar|منطقة توهوكو|az|Tohoku regionu|azb|توهوکو بؤلگه‌سی|ban|Wawengkon Tōhoku|bcl|Rehiyon Tōhoku|be|Тахоку|bg|Тохоку|bn|তোওহোকু অঞ্চল|ca|Regió de Tōhoku|ckb|ناوچەی تۆھۆکو|cs|Tóhoku|cy|Tōhoku|da|Tōhoku|de|Tōhoku|eo|Tōhoku|es|Región de Tōhoku|et|Tōhoku|eu|Tōhoku eskualdea|fa|منطقه توهوکو|fi|Tōhoku|fr|Région du Tōhoku|frr|Tōhoku|ga|Tōhoku|gl|Rexión de Tōhoku|hak|Tōhoku|he|טוהוקו|hi|तोहोकू क्षेत्र|hr|Tōhoku|hu|Tóhoku|hy|Տոհոկու (տարածաշրջան)|id|Wilayah Tōhoku|ilo|Rehion ti Tōhoku|is|Tōhoku|it|Tōhoku|ja|東北地方|ka|ტოჰოკუ|km|តំបន់ថូហុគឹ|ko|도호쿠 지방|la|Tōhoku|lt|Tohoku regionas|lv|Tohoku reģions|mk|Тохоку|mr|तोहोकू|ms|Kawasan Tōhoku|my|တိုးဟိုခု ဒေသ|nl|Tōhoku (regio)|nn|Tohokuregionen|no|Tōhokuregionen|oc|Tōhoku|pam|Tōhoku labuad|pl|Region Tōhoku|pnb|ٹوہوکو|pt|Tohoku (região)|qu|Tōhoku suyu|ro|Regiunea Tōhoku|ru|Тохоку|sc|Tōhoku|sco|Tōhoku region|sd|ٽوهوڪو ريجن|sh|Tōhoku|si|තෝහොකු කලාපය|simple|Tōhoku region|sk|Tóhoku|sl|Tohoku|sr|Тохоку|su|Wewengkon Tōhoku|sv|Tohoku|th|โทโฮกุ|tl|Tōhoku|tr|Tōhoku|uk|Регіон Тохоку|ur|توہوکو علاقہ|uz|Tōhoku viloyati|vi|Tōhoku|war|Tōhoku (rehiyon)|wuu|东北地方|zh|东北地方|zh_min_nan|Tôhoku tē-hng|zh_yue|東北地方|qid=Q129465}}. Since ancient times it has been a site of {{ill|Mountain worship|Q93697439|qid=Q93697439}} centered on {{ill|Shugendō|ca|Shugendo|cs|Šugendó|de|Shugendō|es|Shugendō|fr|Shugendō|it|Shugendō|ja|修験道|ko|수험도|pl|Shugendō|pt|Shugendō|ru|Сюгэндо|simple|Shugendō|sk|Šugendó|sr|Šugendo|tr|Shugendō|zh|修驗道|qid=Q1483875}}, and still draws many practitioners and worshippers.

=== Enshrined deity ===
*{{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}
Through {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|Q2279088|qid=Q2279088}}, the {{ill|Honji suijaku|Q3080781|qid=Q3080781|lt=original Buddhist ground deity}} of the Gassan deity came to be regarded as {{ill|Amitābha|Q236242|qid=Q236242}}. It can be said to be a Tōhoku characteristic that Amida Nyorai—also the honji-butsu of {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637}}—became the honji-butsu of the Gassan deity identified with Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, and it is thought that the spread of {{ill|Pure Land Buddhism|Q262244|qid=Q262244}} brought Amida worship to Gassan<ref name="kamigami">Edited by Ken'ichi Tanigawa, 'Nihon no Kamigami: Shrines and Sacred Sites 12, Tōhoku and Hokkaidō' (Hakusuisha, June 1984)</ref>. Until the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}, the deity of Gassan was considered Hachiman Daibosatsu<ref name="sanzan">Yasuaki Togawa, 'Dewa Sanzan: History and Culture' (Ikubundō, August 1973)</ref>.

Also, Gassan’s auspicious year is said to be the {{ill|mǎo|Q16662792|qid=Q16662792|lt=Year of the Rabbit}}, and visiting in Rabbit years is said to increase blessings.

=== Origin and history ===
[[ファイル:Gassan.JPG|250px|right|thumb|{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sacred peak}} Gassan]]
[[ファイル:Gassan honguu torii.jpg|250px|right|thumb|Wooden torii at Midagahara]]
[[ファイル:Gassan jinja Gate.JPG|250px|right|thumb|Stone torii<br />Inside the stone torii and stone wall is sacred precinct, so photography is prohibited there. A stone marker for Kanpei Taisha can be seen beyond the torii.]]
[[ファイル:Precincts of Gassan jinja.JPG|250px|right|thumb|Distant view of the shrine<br />Mount Chōkai can be seen in the left background.]]
According to shrine tradition, {{ill|Prince Hachiko|Q7244045|qid=Q7244045}}, the third prince of {{ill|Emperor Sushun|Q349238|qid=Q349238}}, opened {{ill|Mount Haguro|Q3090765|qid=Q3090765|lt=Haguro-san}} in the 1st year of {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}} ({{ill|593|Q33889|qid=Q33889}}), and in the same year opened Mount Gassan and established this shrine. Prince Hachiko is said to have cared deeply for local people and listened to their worries and suffering, and thus came to be called “Nojo-sen”<ref>Also called “Nojo Taishi” or “Nojo Daishi.”</ref>.

However, as far as historical sources indicate, there is no evidence that the founder Nojo-sen and Prince Hachiko were the same person<ref name="sanzan" />. Also, between the 4th year of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|Q357246|qid=Q357246}} ({{ill|700|Q23494|qid=Q23494}}), when {{ill|Iwafuke Palisade|Q11587922|qid=Q11587922}} was repaired for the third time<ref>From the entry for February 19, year 4 of Emperor Monmu (700), in '{{ill|Shoku Nihongi|Q611399|qid=Q611399}}'.</ref>, and the 1st year of {{ill|Wadō (era)|Q1373026|qid=Q1373026}} ({{ill|708|Q23511|qid=Q23511}}), when {{ill|Ideha District|Q11395804|qid=Q11395804}} was established<ref>From the entry for September 28, Wadō 1 (708), in 'Shoku Nihongi'.</ref>, subjugation campaigns north of {{ill|Koshi Province (Japan)|Q1351611|qid=Q1351611}} were carried out; it is thought that climbing the {{ill|Three Mountains of Dewa|Q1155726|qid=Q1155726}} would not have been possible before campaigns against the {{ill|Emishi|Q932574|qid=Q932574}} in Dewa began<ref name="meishou">Edited by Yamagata Prefecture, 'Yamagata Prefecture Report on Historic Sites, Scenic Places, and Natural Monuments, Fascicle 11: Dewa Sanzan' (Meicho Shuppan, June 1974; reprint of 1940 edition)</ref>.

In the 10th month decree of {{ill|Hōki|Q18520676|qid=Q18520676}} 4 ({{ill|773|Q31131|qid=Q31131}}) in the '{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}},' two households of shrine-endowment were assigned to the Gassan deity; this is the first appearance of the Gassan deity in historical records<ref name="kamigami" />.

In the '{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}},' articles about the Gassan deity appear repeatedly, including promotions in {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}. Below are the entries in chronological order:
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 6 ({{ill|864|Q25041|qid=Q25041}}), 2nd month 5th day: the {{ill|Dewa Province|Q876032|qid=Q876032}} deity Gassan no Kami, Senior Fourth Rank Upper, Merit Sixth Class, is promoted to {{ill|Junior Third Rank|ja|従三位|ko|종3위|zh|從三位|qid=Q11071123}}.
* Jōgan 10 ({{ill|868|Q25061|qid=Q25061}}), 4th month 15th day: report from Dewa Province—six {{ill|stone arrowhead|Q11587274|qid=Q11587274}} fell like rain before the two shrines of Gassan and Ōmonoimi in {{ill|Akumi District, Yamagata|Q1155592|qid=Q1155592}}.

* Gangyō 4 ({{ill|880|Q23618|qid=Q23618}}), 2nd month 27th day: both Gassan no Kami (Senior Third Rank Merit Fourth Class) and Ōmonoimi no Kami (Senior Third Rank Merit Third Class) are promoted to {{ill|Junior Second Rank|ja|従二位|ko|종2위|zh|從二位|qid=Q11488721}}.
* {{ill|Ninna|Q1346317|qid=Q1346317}} 1 ({{ill|885|ab|885|af|885|am|885 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|885|ar|885|ary|885|ast|885|avk|885|az|885|azb|۸۸۵ (میلادی)|bcl|885|be|885|be_x_old|885|bg|885|bn|৮৮৫|bpy|মারি ৮৮৫|br|885|bs|885.|ca|885|cdo|885 nièng|ceb|885|ckb|٨٨٥|crh|885|cs|885|csb|885|cv|885|cy|885|da|885|de|885|el|885|eml|885|eo|885|es|885|et|885|eu|885|fa|۸۸۵ (میلادی)|fi|885|fo|885|fr|885|fy|885|ga|885|gan|885年|gd|885|gl|885|he|885|hi|885|hr|885.|ht|885 (almanak jilyen)|hu|885|hy|885|id|885|ilo|885|io|885|is|885|it|885|ja|885年|jv|885|ka|885|kaa|885|kk|885 жыл|ko|885년|la|885|lb|885|lij|885|lmo|885|lt|885 m.|lv|885. gads|map_bms|885|mdf|885|mg|885|mhr|885|mk|885|mr|इ.स. ८८५|mrj|885 и|ms|885|mzn|۸۸۵|nah|885|nap|885|nds|885|new|सन् ८८५|nl|885|nn|885|no|885|nrm|885|nso|885|oc|885|or|୮୮୫|os|885-æм аз|pl|885|pnb|885|pt|885|qu|885|ro|885|ru|885 год|rue|885|sa|८८५|scn|885|sd|885ع|se|885|sh|885.|shn|885|si|885|simple|885|sk|885|sl|885|smn|885|sq|885|sr|885|su|885|sv|885|sw|885|tg|Соли 885|th|พ.ศ. 1428|tk|885|tl|885|tly|885|tr|885|tt|885 ел|uk|885|ur|885ء|uz|885|vec|885|vi|885|war|885|wuu|885年|xmf|885|zh|885年|zh_min_nan|885 nî|zh_yue|885年|qid=Q24894}}), 11th month 21st day: in the previous 6th month 21st day, stone arrowhead rain fell in {{ill|Akita Castle|de|Burg Akita|el|Κάστρο της Άκιτα|es|Castillo de Akita|fa|قلعه آکیتا|fr|Château d'Akita|it|Castello di Akita|ja|秋田城|pt|Castelo de Akita|ru|Акита (замок)|tr|Akita Kalesi|uk|Замок Акіта|zh|秋田城|qid=Q11595283}} and Nishihama of Akumi District in Dewa Province; according to the {{ill|Yin-Yang Bureau|fr|Bureau d'Onmyō|ja|陰陽寮|ko|음양료|zh|阴阳寮|qid=Q11658260}}, this was an omen of conspiracy and warfare. According to the {{ill|Department of Divinities|ca|Jingi-kan|es|Jingikan|fa|اداره امور شینتو|fr|Jingi-kan|id|Jingikan|ja|神祇官|ko|신기관|nl|Jingi-kan|pt|Jingi-kan|ru|Дзингикан|simple|Department of Divinities|tr|Jingi-kan|uk|Дзінґікан|vi|Thần kỳ quan|zh|神祇官|qid=Q2264720}}, it was a curse due to disrespect toward Ōmonoimi no Kami and Gassan no Kami of Akumi District and {{ill|Yuzusame Shrine|ja|由豆佐売神社|qid=Q11577650|lt=Yuzusano-me no Kami}} of {{ill|Tagawa district|ja|田川郡 (羽前国)|qid=Q11576762|lt=Tagawa District}}. Therefore an imperial order was issued to the provincial governor to reverently worship the deities and maintain strict guard.
In {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it was listed as a Myōjin Taisha in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}.' In the same '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}},' “Shuzei-shiki,” 2,000 bundles were granted by the state as ritual expenses for Gassan no Kami and Ōmonoimi no Kami.

As above, in the '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}' and '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki}},' the deity of Gassan (a mountain of Tagawa District) is treated as a deity of Akumi District; this is thought to be because at that stage, shrine buildings were maintained and worship conducted in Akumi District near the {{ill|Kokufu|de|Kokufu|fa|کوکوفو|fr|Kokufu|ja|国府|ko|국부 (일본사)|zh|國府 (日本)|qid=Q1629088}}, together with {{ill|Chōkaisan Ōmonoimi Shrine|Q11173679|qid=Q11173679|lt=Ōmonoimi Shrine}} on {{ill|Mount Chōkai|Q713826|qid=Q713826}}<ref name="kamigami" />.

The exact period is unclear, but likely from the middle Heian period<ref name="kamigami" /> until the Meiji {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, Gassan functioned as a Shugendō training ground as part of Dewa Sanzan. Although no materials confirming mountain opening can be found up to the end of the {{ill|Nara period|af|Nara-tydperk|ar|فترة نارا|bcl|Panahon nin Nara|bg|Нара (период)|bn|নারা যুগ|ca|Període Nara|ckb|سەردەمی نارا|cs|Období Nara|de|Nara-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Νάρα|eo|Epoko de Nara|es|Período Nara|eu|Nara aroa|fa|دوره نارا|fi|Nara-kausi|fr|Époque de Nara|gl|Período Nara|he|תקופת נארה|hr|Nara (razdoblje)|hu|Nara-kor|id|Zaman Nara|it|Periodo Nara|ja|奈良時代|jv|Periodhe Nara|ko|나라 시대|lt|Nara laikotarpis|ml|നാറ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Nara|nl|Naraperiode|nn|Naratida|no|Nara-perioden|oc|Periòde de Nara|pl|Nara (okres)|ps|نارا|pt|Período Nara|ro|Perioada Nara|ru|Период Нара|sh|Nara period|simple|Nara period|sk|Obdobie Nara|sl|Obdobje Nara|sr|Нара период|sv|Naraperioden|th|ยุคนาระ|tl|Panahong Nara|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Nala|tr|Nara Dönemi|uk|Період Нара|ur|نارا دور|vi|Thời kỳ Nara|war|Panahon Nara|wuu|奈良时代|zh|奈良時代|zh_min_nan|Nara sî-tāi|zh_yue|奈良時代|qid=Q189178}}, materials requiring consideration first appear in the Heian period<ref name="meishou" />.

This religious power of Dewa Sanzan gradually flourished into a major power that could be called a great territorial domain. Consequently, from the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд Сэнгоку|bg|Сенгоку|bn|সেনগোকু যুগ|bo|སེན་གོའི་དུས་མཚམས་|ca|Període Sengoku|ckb|سەردەمی سێنگۆکو|cs|Období Sengoku|de|Sengoku-Zeit|eo|Epoko Sengoku|es|Período Sengoku|et|Sengoku ajastu|eu|Sengoku aroa|fa|دوره سنگوکو|fi|Sengoku-kausi|fr|Époque Sengoku|ga|Tréimhse Sengoku|glk|سنگؤکۊ زمات|he|תקופת (日本)|zh_min_nan|Sengoku sî-tāi|zh_yue|戰國時代 (日本)|qid=Q204023|lt=Warring States period}} to the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|ar|فترة أزوتشي-موموياما|ast|Periodu Azuchi-Momoyama|be|Перыяд Адзуці-Мамаяма|bg|Адзучи-Момояма|br|Marevezh Azuchi-Momoyama|ca|Període Azuchi-Momoyama|ckb|سەردەمی ئازوچی-مۆمۆیاما|cs|Období Azuči-Momojama|de|Azuchi-Momoyama-Zeit|eo|Azuĉi-Momojama-epoko|es|Período Azuchi-Momoyama|ja|安土桃山時代|ka|აძუტი-მომოიამა|ko|아즈치모모야마 시대|lt|Momojama laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Azuchi–Momoyama|nl|Azuchi-Momoyamaperiode|no|Azuchi-Momoyama-perioden|pl|Azuchi-Momoyama|pt|Período Azuchi–Momoyama|tr|Azuchi-Momoyama Dönemi|uk|Період Адзуті-Момояма|vi|Thời kỳ Azuchi-Momoyama|wuu|安土桃山时代|zh|安土桃山时代|zh_min_nan|Azuti-Momoyama sî-tāi|zh_yue|安土桃山時代|qid=Q319531}}, it faced intervention by warlords such as the {{ill|Daihōji clan|Q11434351|qid=Q11434351|lt=Mutō clan}}, {{ill|Uesugi clan|Q1150058|qid=Q1150058}}, and {{ill|Mogami clan|Q524625|qid=Q524625}}, who sought to incorporate it into their own power. In particular, {{ill|Mogami Yoshiaki|Q839377|qid=Q839377}} repeatedly crossed Gassan when invading the {{ill|Shōnai Plain|Q11485808|qid=Q11485808}}, and soldiers ravaged the Muro, looted Buddhist images and sacred treasures, and so on. For this reason, at Mount Haguro, Buddhist images and sacred treasures were hidden in a cave at Nozoki west of Gassan, and to keep the secret, management was entrusted as a one-son hereditary duty to Jūyōbō, a married practitioner<ref name="sanzan" />. On the other hand, after the {{ill|Battle of Sekigahara|Q234188|qid=Q234188}}, Mogami Yoshiaki, who controlled {{ill|Shōnai region|Q11485804|qid=Q11485804|lt=Shōnai}} and {{ill|Yuri District, Akita|Q8061492|qid=Q8061492|lt=Yuri}}, repaired and rebuilt Haguro and Gassan to win over Dewa Sanzan<ref name="sanzan" />. One such effort was repair of this shrine’s main sanctuary in {{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 6 ({{ill|1601|Q6725|qid=Q6725}})<ref name="sanzan" />.

Even in the Edo period, Dewa Sanzan drew people’s faith as a place of Shugendō. In {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 2 ({{ill|1689|Q7674|qid=Q7674}}), the haikai master {{ill|Matsuo Bashō|Q5676|qid=Q5676}} visited Dewa Sanzan and worshipped atop Gassan on the 6th day of the 6th month<ref>'Oku no Hosomichi' gives the date as June 8, Genroku 2 (1689), but '{{ill|Sora's Diary|Q1101487|qid=Q1101487}}' by {{ill|Kawai Sora|Q11141924|qid=Q11141924}}, who accompanied Bashō and recorded the journey, gives June 6; this is considered correct.</ref>. In his travelogue '{{ill|Oku no Hosomichi|Q1287971|qid=Q1287971}},' he left the verse: “Kumo no mine / ikutsu kuzurete / tsuki no yama” (“How many cloud-peaks collapse—Moon Mountain”).<ref>A monument of this verse now stands near the summit on the Ubasawa route.</ref>

When the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535|lt=separation order}} was issued in Meiji 1 ({{ill|1868|Q7717|qid=Q7717}}), Dewa Sanzan faced an intense wave of {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|Q702298|qid=Q702298}}. Some {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Buddhist monks}} and {{ill|Yamabushi|Q2309838|qid=Q2309838}} returned to lay status and became Shinto priests, while others attempted suicide in grief over Buddhist decline. Many precious Buddhist images, ritual implements, and sutra scrolls were lost through destruction or scattered after being sold. In Meiji 5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), an edict abolishing Shugendō sects was issued, and it seemed Shugendō in Dewa Sanzan might cease; later, however, surviving yamabushi preserved its lineage through their efforts.

Amid such confusion, separation of Shinto and Buddhism in Dewa Sanzan advanced, and on August 31, Meiji 7 ({{ill|1874|Q7761|qid=Q7761}}), this shrine was ranked as Kokuhei Chūsha under the modern shrine ranking system. It was further promoted to Kanpei Chūsha on April 22, Meiji 18 ({{ill|1885|Q7821|qid=Q7821}}), and to Kanpei Taisha on January 4, {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 3 ({{ill|1914|Q2083|qid=Q2083}}). After the end of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=World War II}}, when the modern shrine rank system was abolished, this shrine became in {{ill|1948|Q5165|qid=Q5165}} (Shōwa 23) a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} under the umbrella of the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

In {{ill|1954|Q18581|qid=Q18581}} (Shōwa 29), as a religious corporation combining this shrine with {{ill|Dewa Shrine|Q11395802|qid=Q11395802}} and {{ill|Yudonosan Shrine|Q11563607|qid=Q11563607}}, '''Dewa Sanzan Shrine''' ('''Sanjin Gōsaiden''') was established on Mount Haguro.
